claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi produced by conventional processing typically has a single-phase, FCC-dominated microstructure.
Controlled solidification or targeted heat treatment, including cooling near 800 °C followed by short-time aging, can produce a fine interpenetrating FCC+BCC microstructure.
The resulting dual-phase microstructure will consist of a ductile FCC matrix containing an embedded BCC reinforcing phase.
Controlled cooling rates and precise aging conditions can produce coherent FCC/BCC interphase boundaries.
Uncontrolled cooling or overaging may produce incoherent interfaces or undesirable phase distributions.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces provide effective load transfer.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces hinder dislocation motion.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces deflect propagating cracks.
The BCC phase supplies high strength to the dual-phase alloy.
The FCC phase preserves ductility in the dual-phase alloy.
Barriers to dislocation motion at coherent interfaces improve yield strength.
Crack deflection at coherent interfaces improves fracture resistance.
The coherent dual-phase structure will maintain or enhance Young's modulus.
The proposed dual-phase samples are expected to have approximately 15% higher yield strength than conventionally processed single-phase HEAs.
The proposed dual-phase samples are expected to have enhanced Young's modulus and fracture toughness while maintaining or marginally improving ductility.
Conventional single-phase HEAs typically exhibit a strength–ductility trade-off and less optimized modulus and fracture resistance.
Loss of interphase coherency, excessive BCC content, or brittle secondary-phase formation will compromise the proposed property synergy.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says ductility will be enhanced, whereas the predicted outcome permits ductility merely to be maintained.
